speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a serious symptom that requires immediate investigation. To determine the cause, can you tell me if you noticed any abdominal distension or if the vomiting contains blood or bile?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus.

The combination of bilious vomiting in a newborn, especially with a family history of pyloric stenosis, is highly suspicious for this surgical emergency. Given the severity of the symptoms and the age of the patient, immediate surgical consultation and preparation for an emergency upper GI contrast study are required.
